title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Sequential and Ecological Program for Sustainable Resilience of the Sila Populations programme will work in Sila Province, Chad. It aims to contribute to Concern Chad's Green Graduation thematic programme, and the goal of the grant is to ensure extremely poor and vulnerable households are more productive, can sustainably meet their basic needs and have improved coping strategies through strengthened livelihoods which place value on the natural environment. The programme will support over 110,970 people living in extreme poor households, subsistence farmers, pastoralists, female-headed households, households with disabled members. This will be done through ensuring access to a predictable and regular source of income to cover basic needs, increased access to basic services, improved knowledge of labour market opportunities, increased employment among participant households including in jobs focused on prevention or restoring the environment.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: Improved food and livelihood security and nutritional status for affected people in Ngouboua sub department, Kaya, Tchad . SPECIFIC OUTCOME: DRR 1: HH resilience to shocks or disasters is strengthened as the programme works with formal financial service providers on the risk that people living in conditions of extreme poverty pose as clients and tailoring suitable products and services or establishing bridging structures through community-based savings groups.Aid to Environment 1: Concern’s Green Graduation programme added a 5th pillar to the traditional graduation model - the ‘green’ aspect which aims to improve environmental protection and stability through awareness raising, capacity building, assessing environmental impacts, reducing and managing environmental risks and increasing natural assets.Capacity Building 1: Participants' capacity is built through training such as on financial management, vocational skills, and business skills.Gender Equality 1: a gender lens is applied at every stage and a gender transformative approach is taken to tackle harmful gender norms, attitudes and practices.Nutrition 1: Through increased financial security and messaging on nutrition, the nutritional status of HHs is improved.
